sources.entry: BlockBlock - Me: "Please alert me whenever anything is persistently installed." BlockBlock: "You got it" [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/objective-see/BlockBlock)

summary.name: BlockBlock
summary.one_liner: BlockBlock is a macOS tool from Objective-See that monitors common persistence locations and alerts you when a new persistent component is added.
use_cases: Alerting when software installs itself to run at login or restart
Reviewing and allowing or blocking persistent items on a Mac
Blocking non-notarized or downloaded scripts from running
Checking processes and persistent items against VirusTotal
summary.what_it_does: BlockBlock monitors common macOS persistence locations and displays an alert whenever a new persistent component is added. Each alert shows the responsible process (name, pid, path, arguments) and the persistent item installed, with options for code signing info, VirusTotal lookups, and process ancestry. Users can allow or block events, and those responses become rules that can be viewed and deleted in a rules window. Optional protections include Notarization mode (blocks non-notarized programs, by default only downloaded ones), Block Script mode (blocks downloaded scripts), and Paste Protection (added in version 2.3) which checks pastes into Terminal. It uses Apple's Endpoint Security Framework and logs alert responses to /Library/Objective-See/BlockBlock/BlockBlock.log.
notable: Alerts on new persistence (launch items, login items and similar) and shows process details, code signing, VirusTotal links and ancestry
Optional Notarization, Block Script and Paste Protection modes; Paste Protection targets ClickFix attacks in Terminal
Open source, with source code on GitHub (linked from awesome-mac listing)
Logs alert responses to a local file
caveats: Requires system privileges, Full Disk Access and Accessibility permission (for Paste Protection) to be granted manually
Alerts do not necessarily mean infection; legitimate software also persists
On macOS Ventura a macOS bug caused 'BlockBlock Not Active' alerts; fixed in macOS 13.0.1 or via a manual workaround
Responses to alerts for notarized processes are not saved across reboots
